fact: FIJ reports that a birth record on the NPC's VitalReg digital birth registration portal was found registered under a Lagos man's National Identification Number (NIN), linking birth records to the NIN.

UNICEF's Denis Onoise said health-facility interoperability between birth registration and the national identity system had stalled, with none of 371 targeted facilities live at the time of the assessment, while NPC and NIMC propose that NIMC link registered births to the identity database and assign the NIN.
system: health-facility interoperability of birth registration with the NIN system

fact: The NPC says it now generates a NIN for each child at birth registration and synchronises birth registration data with NIMC's NIN records.
The NPC release says NPC, the Health Ministry, NIMC and Barnksforte Technologies have an initiative to issue a national identification number to every child at birth, starting in 2024.

The NPC chairman said the NIN has been integrated into the e-CRVS system and newborns can now receive a NIN at birth. Per the NPC chairman, birth certificates in Jigawa are processed for NIN generation.

UNICEF says Nigeria's electronic birth registration, signed under a January 2025 compact with the NPC, NIMC and others, has interoperability between birth records, health information systems and the National Identification Number as a key feature.
NPC, NIMC, UNICEF and ALGON agreed a compact for ward-level static points issuing birth certificates and NINs to under-fives, with data interoperability, in eleven pilot states.
system: Ward-level birth registration and NIN enrolment points

fact: President Tinubu said NIMC had harmonised and linked data with 125 partner agencies, including the National Population Commission for birth registration.

Nigeria 24 reports that the National Population Commission's launched VitalReg platform integrates with the National Identity Management Commission, and self-service birth registration requires the child to already hold a National Identification Number.

The Lagos e-Birth registration platform, launched 13 November 2025 by UNICEF and the Lagos State Government, automatically links a newborn to a National Identification Number where at least one parent already has one, the NPC's Lagos commissioner says.
